title: Anne Wojcicki, the FDA's Warning Letter and Fifteen Months of Steps
conflicts: Wojcicki gave two accounts of what the company knew (PLOS 2015: originally thought no FDA approval needed; KQED 2015: understood by 2010 it would be a regulated device); both are given as hers, in sequence. Engadget first reported refunds, then corrected; refunds are left out. Customer numbers differ (13m per AP court documents vs 15m per ABC in 2025) and are not used. Sale-approval day differs (Friday 27 June per AP vs Monday per ABC); the story says 'that summer'.
notes: Told as the 2013 letter, the 5 December 2013 compliance decision and the road to the February 2015 Bloom syndrome authorisation, with the October 2015 relaunch, April 2017 authorisation and the 2025 bankruptcy and sale to TTAM as factual aftermath without blame. FDA documents are cited from Internet Archive copies (current fda.gov URLs are 404). The reflection touches validation and answering regulators without mentioning talQen.
